This issue might be a duplicate of an existing issue. Please check:
- #26966: Same bug — `opencode web` resolves working directory to system/drive root instead of the CWD where the command was invoked (previously reported on Windows, this report is on macOS)
This will be sweet, I want the agent to be able to do its own token budgeting.

Same use case here — I run multiple OpenCode GO accounts for rate limit headroom, but the only way to use them is manually swapping keys via `/connect` or editing `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json`.

What I really need is: **same-provider key-level rotation**, not just model-to-model fallback. When the current GO key hits 429, rotate to the next GO key automatically within the same request.

This would also benefit people who:
- Have multiple ChatGPT Plus/Pro accounts
- Use multiple API keys from the same provider (e.g., OpenAI org keys)
- Run GO + Zen simultaneously as a budget/fallback pair

The auth-v2 proposal (#5748) had the right idea with `same-request rotation` — would love to see that land as part of this model fallback feature.

Fixed for V2 by #34843, including ChatGPT OAuth routing through the Codex backend and regression coverage for routing, missing account IDs, non-ChatGPT OAuth, and model eligibility. The provider-owned follow-up is tracked separately in #35212. Closing as implemented.

Most of this tracker has landed via #34619, #34665, #34946, and #34956: Effect plugins can register tools, the canonical tool type is plugin-owned, built-ins use the same registration path, and registration/materialization are tested.

Keeping this open with narrower remaining scope: config-discovered Promise plugins still have no `ctx.tool` API (`packages/plugin/src/v2/promise/context.ts` and `packages/core/src/plugin/promise.ts`). #34709 and #34805 are adjacent work, not blockers for the already-complete Effect-side architecture.

Progressive read-triggered discovery is implemented and tested by `d972aa9d83` and `bea6e1499d`: path-local `AGENTS.md` files are discovered, root instructions are excluded, and prior admissions are deduplicated.

Keeping this open with narrower remaining scope because the chosen admission architecture is not implemented. The current path emits durable synthetic user messages directly; it does not contribute a session-scoped `SystemContext.Source`, reconcile through the context checkpoint, or provide capability-aware native System lowering as specified here.

Implemented by #34941 and refined by #34945. Embedders now have persisted per-session keyed entries with put/replace, remove, and list APIs. Entries project through System Context, changes and removals become chronological updates, and the checkpoint/compaction lifecycle preserves current context across compaction. Closing as implemented.

#34558 fixed the immediate failure mode and added coverage: GPT/OpenAI models receive `apply_patch`, while other models receive `edit`/`write`.

Keeping this open for the unresolved design: replace the hardcoded provider/model check with configurable policy, define composition and precedence across model/provider/agent/plugin inputs, and decide whether unavailable tools require client representation.

Implementation is consolidated in #35272: explicit execution lifecycle events, structured retry projection, interruption reasons, and visible content-filter failure handling. Rich extensible error details were split to #35325. Keeping this open until #35272 merges.

Tracker status: completed audit work is mapped to merged PRs, with execution/retry/fragments/settlement cleanup consolidated in #35272. Guidance summaries and terminology remain independently tracked by #35017 and #35057. Keep open until #35272 merges, then this can close under the tracker’s “complete or intentionally split” criterion.

Implementation is consolidated in #35272: text/reasoning IDs are removed from the Session contract, provider continuation metadata becomes opaque state, tool `callID` remains, and the publisher enforces one active text/reasoning fragment per step. Keeping this open until #35272 merges.

The remaining body items are consolidated in #35272: tool settlement ordering and continuation-oriented compaction headings. Separate `text`/`recent`, derived compaction message IDs, and the accepted synthetic metadata shape are already in place. Failed-compaction terminal handling remains independently tracked by #34919. Keeping this open until #35272 merges.

Confirmed this race remains on the current V2 branch. #35267 implements the readiness barrier and regression coverage, but is still open with failing Linux and Windows unit CI. Keeping this issue open until that PR lands successfully.

Narrowing this to the still-unimplemented structured `changes` payload and its source/item metadata. Terminology, event naming, projected message naming, and API renames are tracked separately in #35057. The preparatory #35045 branch was closed unmerged.

Replacement semantics are still present and covered by tests, so the design question remains open. #34941 now gives embedders an additive per-session context seam, while #34721 tracks the concrete agent-system bug.

The remaining scope here is the agent configuration contract: explicit override versus additive instructions, ordering relative to provider and durable context, and whether the effective prompt stack needs inspection/debug visibility.
This primary happens all the time in Kimi V2.7 code, but I'd imagine it could happen to any LLM that had this bad pattern for whatever reason.

> 
> So you mean would be better to also give the agent context from the sub agents? I don't really think it would be a good idea, the point of sub-agents is to do tasks without flooding the parent agent's context, imagine a case where someone has 7 sub-agents running, giving their context to the parent agent would eat up a lot of it's context...
> 
> I think it might be good to give the agent the error that happened so the sub-agent was aborted, however it might be an API request error to provider, and I guess agent might hallucinate stuff up on it
> 
> Let me know if I misunderstood you or you have something else in mind

I'm proposing that when the last message in a subagent session is not an assistant text return, present that with a notice to the primary agent so it can understand that: 1) the subagent did work the task, but got interrupted, stalled, or errored out, 2) based upon the text showing the error message or stall nature can decide if resuming the session is the best course of action, or task a fresh session, or investigate the failure prior to any further tasking.

I think if we give the agent the message type and middle-truncate messages to a set character limit, it'll be information that helps agents more efficiently resolve a somewhat common failure pattern. That overall, it's less costly to supply the data than have the agent operate without it.

The hallucination risk can be addressed by packaging the subagent-tail message and it's message-type data as part of an agent return. Proper message labeling, such as 'Agent Return Failure • the agent did not issue return text. The last text in the agents session is: {message-type: middle-truncated text block}.

While developing a plugin that modifies session context prior to sending to the provider API, built off a fork of DCP, I have observed If you inject session context utilization info labeled as "context-info" as a synthetic tool part, the agent hallucinates having called a "context-info" tool. Move it to being a user message, and label it as as system directive, and provide a system prompt that informs the agent 'this text with this format is a system notice from the environment', and it doesn't confuse it coming from the user and properly uses the injected information as environmental data. 

I would expect the wording of the Agent Return Failure notice would be sufficient by itself. Adding a concise 1-2 sentence instruction explaining what an Agent Return Failure is to the task tool prompt could be an additive safeguard.

I can reproduce this on OpenCode 1.17.13 with Ollama 0.22.1.

Environment:
- OpenCode 1.17.13
- Ollama 0.22.1
- Debian 13
- Intel Core i5-1035G4
- 16 GB RAM

Configuration:
- Provider: @ai-sdk/openai-compatible
- Base URL: http://localhost:11434/v1
- Model: gemma4:e2b-32k

Steps to reproduce:
1. Restart Ollama.
2. Start OpenCode.
3. Select gemma4:e2b-32k.
4. Send a single prompt:
   "Say OK"

Expected:
The model should immediately answer "OK".

Actual:
OpenCode never returns a response.

Observations:
- While OpenCode is hanging, `ollama ps` shows gemma4:e2b-32k running at 100% CPU.
- If I send a second request using curl to `/v1/chat/completions` while OpenCode is still waiting, that request also hangs.
- After restarting Ollama, the exact same curl request succeeds.
- `/v1/chat/completions` works correctly outside OpenCode.
- Both `stream: false` and `stream: true` work correctly with curl.

Example:

curl http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model":"gemma4:e2b-32k",
    "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say OK"}],
    "stream":true
  }'

Response times after restarting Ollama:
- first request: ~21 s
- second request: ~8 s

The problem only appears after OpenCode sends its request. It looks like the request issued by OpenCode causes Ollama to stop completing subsequent chat requests until Ollama is restarted.
